mutants.why: high nibble must shift by 4; a wrong shift decodes every =XX byte to the wrong value
the first hex digit sits at +1; reading +2 decodes the wrong nibble
the second hex digit sits at +2; reading +1 decodes the wrong nibble
shifting the high nibble right instead of left collapses it to zero, corrupting every decoded byte
a bare CR after = must skip only the CR (advance 1); treating CR-or-LF as CRLF over-consumes the following byte
SECURITY: without AbortOnBase64DecodingErrors Qt silently yields a partial decode for malformed base64, so a truncated attacker body is handed onward as if complete instead of failing closed
SECURITY: a strict-base64 decode failure must report ok==false; returning ok==true lets the caller treat a failed decode as a valid empty body
Content-Transfer-Encoding tokens are case-insensitive per RFC 2045; a case-sensitive match sends a 'BASE64' part through undecoded
val1 is shifted left by 4 so its low nibble is zero, and val2 is a single hex digit (0..15); OR and ADD produce the identical byte for every input, so no test can (or should) distinguish them
